learning_outcomes.description: Be able to plan, develop and carry out an independent research project.
Obtain an in-depth knowledge of the specific topic area through a thorough literature review.
Develop research skills and be able to locate and use information sources.
Present results of research in a written thesis.
Present results of research in an oral seminar.

assessments.task_description: Write a research proposal of up to, but not more than, one page, describing the background and aims of your project. Make sure you include the project title, your name, and that of your supervisor/s. Please show this to your supervisor/s before you submit it.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submit pdf via email (or other method by prior arrangement) to the Course Coordinator.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: Students who are unable to arrange a supervisor and complete the outline of research by the end of Week 2 should consider withdrawing from the course. Please contact the Course Coordinator for advice.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
Approximately half-way through their project, students will give a roughly 15 minute talk on their masters project to their research group, and expert examiner if possible. The presentation will be given in-person or via video-conferencing, as appropriate at the time. Show your supervisor(s) a draft of the talk, and practise your talk with your peers before presenting to the group.

The supervisor and student co-ordinate to choose a convenient time for the research group and expert examiner, preferably within the last week of the student's first semester on the project.

The student will enable feedback from the audience using the oral presentation feedback form available via Blackboard.
assessments.submission_guidelines: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.
assessments.additional_info: You cannot defer or apply for an extension for this assessment.

assessments.task_description:
Each student will submit a written progress report. Discuss in detail with your supervisor the progress that has been made and what steps are needed to finish the project, as well as an appropriate format for the report. The report should include a comprehensive background and literature review in a form appropriate for inclusion in the thesis. Include the background theory needed for a non-expert to understand your project. The report should also include a description of the progress of the research work to date and a brief plan for the rest of the project.

Length is typically 10-15 pages.

The style of writing and referencing should be the same as that expected for the thesis.

You can write your report in whatever format you like (TeX, Word, etc). Discuss with your supervisor what may be appropriate. A thesis template, which you may find useful, is available.

Show a draft of the report to your supervisor(s) for their feedback before you submit it.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submit pdf via email (or other method by prior arrangement) to Course Coordinator.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: You will receive a mark of 0 if this assessment is submitted late.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
At the end of their project students will give a 20 minute oral presentation on their Masters project to the entire Physics department. The presentation will be given in person or online, as appropriate at the time. The presentation is immediately followed by a maximum of 5 minutes of question-and-answer with the audience.

Discuss a draft of your Masters Talk with your supervisor(s), and practice your talk with your peers.

Both expert and non-expert examiners are expected to see the Masters Talk, either in-person or via videoconference. The course coordinator schedules the talks of all students, aiming to organise so that both examiners can see, live, the presentation of the project they are assessing.

This assessment item will be audio-visually recorded and retained in accordance with University requirements.

This assessment item is not eligible for a remark due to it being independently marked by two examiners.

assessments.task_description:
At the end of the course, each student will submit a written thesis and subsequently undertake a final talk and oral examination.

The thesis is due by 5:00 pm on Monday of the first week of the examination period. The final talk and oral examination must be held after submission of the thesis and before the end of the examination period. The exact date and time should be arranged by the student in consultation with the supervisor, and the two additional examiners: a subject-matter expert and a non-specialist examiner.

The thesis should introduce the project and explain its motivation and the broader context of the research field. It should demonstrate familiarity with the relevant literature. The literature review submitted halfway through the year will likely provide the basis for this part of the thesis.

The description of the project should be sufficiently detailed to allow a new student to understand how the work was conducted and, where appropriate, reproduce it using the information provided. The thesis must clearly identify which aspects of the project were completed by the student.

The research results should be presented clearly and interpreted critically. The student should explain how the findings relate to the current state of research in the area. The conclusion may also discuss possible extensions of the project and directions for future work.

The expected length of the thesis is approximately 50 pages. This is a guideline rather than a strict requirement. Heavily theoretical theses may be shorter, whereas experimental theses containing many plots or substantial amounts of data may be longer. Conciseness and clarity are valued by the assessors, and a densely written thesis may communicate the required material in fewer pages.

A Physics thesis template is available and may be used in preparing the thesis.

Students are strongly encouraged to submit a draft of the thesis to their supervisor or supervisors for feedback well before the submission deadline, normally at least one week before the final talk.

Students who believe that they may be unable to submit the thesis by the deadline because of extenuating circumstances should contact both their supervisor or supervisors and the course coordinator as soon as the circumstances become apparent.
assessments.submission_guidelines: Submit pdf of the Thesis via email (or other method by prior arrangement) to Course Coordinator.
assessments.deferral_or_extension: You may be able to apply for an extension.
assessments.late_submission: A penalty of 1 grade for each 24 hour period from time submission is due will apply for up to 7 days. After 7 days you will receive a mark of 0.
assessments.additional_info: You may be able to apply for an extension.

assessments.task_description:
During the exam period after you hand in your report you will attend (either in person or online via Zoom or similar video conferencing technology) an oral examination with the examiners and your project supervisor. You will need to discuss a suitable date and venue with your project supervisor, examiners, and course coordinator.

The examination will be conducted by a panel of three examiners:

  • the project supervisor;
  • an examiner with expertise relevant to the project; and
  • a non-specialist examiner.

The examination will normally last approximately 20–40 minutes. At the beginning of the examination, the student will give a brief presentation of approximately 10 minutes, summarising the project’s motivation, aims, methods, principal results, and conclusions. The remainder of the examination will consist of questions from the panel.

Students are expected to demonstrate an understanding of the complete thesis, including material developed collaboratively or with guidance from the supervisor. Questions will not be limited to material covered in the opening presentation.

Questions may address:

  • the motivation, aims, and scientific context of the project;
  • the student’s individual contribution to the work;
  • the theoretical, experimental, or computational methods used;
  • the reasons for important methodological or analytical decisions;
  • the interpretation, reliability, and limitations of the results;
  • the relationship between the results and the existing literature;
  • alternative interpretations or approaches;
  • possible improvements, extensions, or future directions; and
  • the communication of the project to both specialist and non-specialist audiences.


This assessment item will be audio-visually recorded and retained in accordance with University requirements.

This assessment item is not eligible for a remark due to it being independently marked by two examiners.
